title: Bad restriction weight and switching probability
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\varphi$ be a disjunctive normal form on $n$ sign variables, and let $\delta$ be real. The total weight, under the product restriction weights with free-coordinate weight $\delta$ and each fixed-sign weight $(1-\delta)/2$, of restrictions on which $\varphi$ is nonconstant equals the coordinate-switching failure probability at threshold $1$ for the Boolean function represented by $\varphi$.
hypotheses_covered: A disjunctive normal form on those coordinates
